lines.trans: Two black came up, we lost everything again.
Ah, and I wanted to bet on two!
That's it, my money is completely down to zero.
Make a quick currency exchange for me, please.
Samson, you are also already at zero after all.
That's it, let's leave here quickly onto the street.
Wait, I must win back our money!
Get up from the chair, do not lose your mind.
Samson never surrenders just like that!
Calm down, let us go outside into fresh air now.
Alright, everything is fine, I am already calm.
Let's go, we need to think urgently about what next.

Outdoor environment. Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'здух'). Common masculine noun meaning 'air; outdoors' in everyday Russian.

вставать.gloss: to get up, to stand up

meanings.note: Out of bed or from the floor. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тавать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to get up, to stand up', paired with 'встать'.
Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тавать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to get up, to stand up', paired with 'встать'.

examples.trans: Come on, Tuzik, let's get up!
I get up at seven in the morning.
Come on, Tuzik, let's get up!

meanings.note: Takes из + genitive. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'пасть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fall out', paired with 'выпадать'.

examples.text: Я не выходил! Я выпал из окна!
examples.trans: I didn't walk out! I fell out the window!
The first snow fell during the night.

examples.text: Ещё раз вам говорю, я не выходил! Я выпал из окна!
examples.trans: I'm telling you again, I didn't walk out! I fell out the window!

meanings.note: In a list or a story. Core Russian adv meaning 'next; further' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: The number or digit 2. Common feminine noun meaning 'two; number two; failing grade' in everyday Russian.

Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Agreeing, often reluctantly. Core Russian part meaning 'all right, OK' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Colloquial. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.

meanings.note: Locative / directional adverb. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'сюда').

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: To recover losses through playing. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ыграть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to win back; to recover', paired with 'отыгрывать'.

To perform a game or match. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ыграть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to win back; to recover', paired with 'отыгрывать'.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Food, air, news. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вежий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fresh').

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.
examples.trans: Fresh berries, coffee! You are having a romantic breakfast here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'даваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give up, to surrender', paired with 'сдаться'.

examples.text: Никогда не сдавайся! Сегодня я выйду отсюда под подписку!
examples.trans: Never give up! Today I'm getting out of here on a travel ban!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: comparative of скоро used as adverb or particle

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нова').

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!

meanings.note: Совсем не. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').
Совсем не. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

meanings.note: Спокойной ночи = good night. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('calm, quiet').

examples.text: Это ваша самоуверенность промелькнула. Спокойной ночи!

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.en: to put, to place in an upright position
meanings.note: Takes accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тавить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to put, to place', paired with 'поставить'.

examples.trans: Where should I put the plate?
Put the kettle on the table.

examples.text: Успокойтесь, я ещё сделаю! Куда ставить тарелку?
examples.trans: Calm down, I'll make more! Where should I put the plate?

meanings.note: Irregular plural стулья. Common masculine noun meaning 'chair' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And why do we need a log? I brought folding chairs right here!

meanings.en: to go and come back, to pop over
meanings.note: 'Сходите!' = Go on, go and see. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (somewhere and come back)', paired with 'ходить'.

examples.trans: Yes, go on. Don't mix it up with another one!

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.
